doc.title: Jim Galloway interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Playing small groups in Glasgow, art school and Monk tunes
summary: He emigrated in 1964; before that he played small traditional groups around Glasgow, including an art-school quintet playing Thelonious Monk tunes.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Cool. What playing — you moved to Canada in what year?
It’s a sort of personal statement.
You must have done a certain amount of playing in Scotland before you came over here.
Oh yeah, yeah, I did a lot of playing.
Was it in small groups or big bands?

No it was small groups. Small groups. I played, I mean in the late 50s, jazz had a huge revival over there, it was on the charts. I mean there was all kinds of traditionally- oriented music that was hit parade music, so there was quite a lot of work. And well I played mostly around the Glasgow area, and with a lot of different groups. And the styles of the band were pretty traditional, although at one time I went to art school in Glasgow, and while I was in art school I had this quintet, with a very close friend of mine who went to art school with me, his name was Andy Park, he ended up in television. But this quintet, it was baritone, trombone, piano, bass, drums, and we played Monk music, Thelonious Monk tunes.
Yeah. So as I say I’ve always had a very sort of broad acceptance of the music. And nowadays in my leisure time I listen a lot to classical, because it’s another aspect of music.
